releases.displayName: Minor bug fix - Involuntary movement bug finally fixed

items.text: Fixed a rare but very annoying and game breaking issue that only affected some users, where the character would move in circles/on their own.: This bug was extremely difficult to catch because I was never able to reproduce it on my own. When a player commented about it recently, I decided to take another look since it had been a while. Heartworm uses Unity's new Input System, and I saw that we had set as composite bindings in the Move and Turn actions. After looking into it, I found that it's unlikely was actually ever used for any real input, and more than likely was picking up any HID device or driver - including virtual devices registered via driver software (audio, rgb, macros, etc.). Unity was likely guessing an axis center for these devices, normalizing it, and the result was the character moving seemingly on its own.: Again, due to the nature of this bug and my inability to reproduce it, I can't personally confirm the fix, but the player who reported it most recently confirmed the fix worked for them on a test branch, so I am pushing it live. If for some reason you run into this issue after updating, please let me know.: Thanks,: Vincent

releases.displayName: Unity Security Update/Small Bug Fix Patch

items.text: Hi all,

Due to the recently found potential security vulnerability in some Unity versions (https://unity.com/security/sept-2025-01) I had to update the engine version, so that is the main focus of this build. I don't believe the game was effected, but I updated just to be safe. I did some testing, but there is the possibility that this introduces unexpected issues. I hope it's not the case but please let me know if you find anything weird.
Fixed player controls issue after LTS update - Enabled "input consumption" which is a new project setting that was added by the LTS update
Fixed camera mods being deleted if you saved/loaded while camera was unequipped or stored in item box
Fixed face material not changing in spider outro cutscene for certain costumes (i.e. tapekeeper costume)
Fixed Statue enemy damage hitbox not being disabled sometimes after defeating them
Vincent
An issue was reported where sometimes loading the game would lead to a black screen.
A player submitted their save file and I was able to solve the issue - turns out there was a minor reference error I had missed when adding the new camera mod.
This hot fix should solve it.
Vincent
You can also now purchase the game’s soundtrack - featuring 60 original songs written for the game.

As previously mentioned, with this update, there is a new, optional increased difficulty called “Challenge” mode, with a new costume reward upon completion. This will require much stricter management of resources and more careful decision-making in regard to when to fight or flee. (The original, normal difficulty of the game still exists, of course.)
There are also a number of other additions and changes, outlined below:

Hey Everyone!
As we close out the year and move towards the launch of Heartworm next year, we wanted to start showing off more of the game to get everyone excited for Sam's journey through the unknown.

In case you missed it, we refreshed the demo after PAX to include the new boss fight and make the demo experience a better representation of the game. This latest version features improved textures from the original demo, the ability to enhance your camera with mods, and, most excitingly, a chance to play one of the boss fights from the game.
Let's get a look at what we're here to talk about.
If you've played either version of the demo, you're likely very familiar with The Neighborhood. But did you know there are still areas left to explore?

When Sam enters Platt St. Deli, the rush of memories is instant. The store is so familiar—the shelves lined with cereal, the scent of fresh-cut meat, the soft chime of the bell above the door. This was where her Grandfather once worked, and Sam has so many fond memories of this place. But being back here now, she can't seem to find those fond memories; instead, she only feels the sadness as she's reminded yet again of what he's gone.

The Static Wraiths shudder and warp as they trudge, their shifting masses of discordant distortion ceaselessly pulsing to an unnatural rhythm. They wander, ever emitting their mournful hum, the fading echoes of memories slipping away. Each one, visitor lost to this place—every flicker and buzz an an echoing reminder of loss- of refusal to let go.

The Static Wraith attacks by releasing a flow of static. As the static flows over Sam, it slows their movement. The longer Sam is caught in the static, the more sluggish she becomes. The Wraith uses this moment to close the gap, forcing Sam to overcome the static and fight back before it can strike.

Hey Everyone!
It's been a while since we've updated everyone on the progress that's been made in Heartworm, so we wanted to keep you all in the loop!

In case you missed it, we showcased a fresh, updated demo at PAX! This new version featured improved textures from the original demo, the ability to enhance the camera with mods, and, most excitingly, a thrilling boss fight from the game.
In addition to showcasing the demo, we also wanted to give you a glimpse of some new environments you'll be able to explore in the game beyond The Neighborhood!
During Sam's journey, they will find themselves lost in the dense Wilderness. What truths wait down the trail?
As a comparison, here's a screenshot showing the pixelated filter on/off

"I was so happy to be able to show off the new demo at PAX West and even more so to watch people enjoy it. Admittedly I am always pretty nervous showing off the game, but that melted away so quickly as I met and talked to everyone who is excited about Heartworm. A lot of you had positive things to say and great feedback - it's really inspiring to hear how excited people are for this game and how passionate they are about the genre. Can't wait to show you more." - Vincent.
